title: What is known about 1RB---_0RC0RD_1LD0RF_0LE0LC_1RA0LC_1RC0RA
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB---_0RC0RD_1LD0RF_0LE0LC_1RA0LC_1RC0RA.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. The machine works a stack of blocks at the right end of the tape; Lean proves its two working modes for all block lengths. Each pop makes the top about 2.5 times larger and moves the deeper blocks by a few cells, so what happens when a deep block empties is far beyond simulation.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (A1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 76,226 cells have been visited and 55,302 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: fixed/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape stopped growing in the second half of the run (bounded so far, or growing so slowly that no record fell in the last half). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.524).

claims.title: The two working modes
claims.text: Mode A: 1^(x+2) (01)^y 0 F> becomes 1^x (01)^(y+2) 0 F> at the next visit of the right end; mode B: 1^(x+4) (01)^(y+1) 0010 (01)^z 0 F> becomes 1^x (01)^(y+3) 0010 (01)^(z+1) 0 F>; for all values and any tape to the left.

claims.title: The modes cover almost every visit
claims.text: Of the 38,033 visits of the head to the right end in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps, the mode rules predict 37,795 exactly and none wrongly; the other 238 are pops and small cases.

claims.title: A hierarchy of counters
claims.text: Each pop multiplies the top by about 2.5, and the block two levels down changes by 4 cells every two pops; it needs about 240 more pops to run out, when the top would be about 2.5<sup>240</sup> cells long.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. The decider pipeline of bbchallenge left it open; no proof either way is recorded here yet.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. The machine works a stack of counters at the right end of its tape; every time the top one runs out the next one starts about 2.5 times larger, and the deeper ones tick far too slowly for any simulation to see them empty.

facts.text: the steady work at the right end, proved in Lean for all block lengths.
growth of the top block; the deep blocks change by a few cells per cycle.
No halt in the C simulator; 76,226 cells visited.
No halt, proved in Lean; the first 10,000 by the kernel alone.

sections.heading: A stack of blocks
html: The left part of the tape is a record of the past; the work happens at the right end. The tape is a stack of blocks 1^u (01)^v separated by 00. Each time the head, in state F, reaches the right end, the top block is in one of two modes:

• mode A, 1^X (01)^Y 0: two 1s become two more 01 pairs;
  • mode B, 1^X (01)^Y 0010 (01)^Z 0: four 1s become two more pairs, and one more pair is added after the marker 0010.

When the 1s are used up, the head goes down the stack: the pairs of the top become the 1s of a new top, about twice as many, and the blocks just below change a little. One pop of each kind multiplies the top by about 2.5: 1,227 → 3,069 → 7,679 → 19,199 → 47,999.

sections.heading: Counters inside counters
html: The block two levels below the top, 1^W (01)^V, loses 4 ones and gains 2 pairs every two pops (W = 975, 971, 967, …). It is a counter ticking once per cycle of the level above, and the level above it ticks once per cycle of the top. When a lower level changes, the tops can shrink for a while (12,933 → 6,451 → 3,211 → 1,591 → 781) before they grow again.

The level-two block needs about 240 more pops to run out; by then the top would be about 2.5240 cells long. Whether the machine halts depends on what the deep levels do when they empty, which no simulation will reach.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape stopped growing in the second half of the run (bounded so far, or growing so slowly that no record fell in the last half). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.524).
After 109 steps the tape spans 76,226 cells (13 left of the start, 59,028 right), with a density of 1s of 0.726.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

summary: A stack of counters at the right end: the top block is converted two or four cells per visit, and each pop starts a top about 2.5 times larger while the deeper blocks tick slowly (open).
